evals.prompt: Recreate the provided spaceship raster as a clean, maintainable SVG. Use agent-svgtools to evaluate and improve the result, but do not use automatic trace. Save spaceship.svg and a brief worklog.md listing the commands you ran and your final assessment. You may create any other artifacts useful to your workflow. Visually verify the finished SVG.
evals.expected_output: A recognizable, visually faithful spaceship expressed as concise maintainable vector geometry, with enough command evidence to verify how agent-svgtools was used.
expectations: The requested SVG and work log exist, and the SVG renders successfully at 500 by 500 pixels.
The SVG has a 0 0 500 500 viewBox, preserves transparency, and contains no image element, data URL, embedded raster, script, or external resource.
The SVG uses no more than 20 authored graphical elements, no more than 12 path elements, and no more than 60 path commands.
At least three visible components have meaningful ids or belong to meaningfully named groups, and the intentional fill/stroke palette contains no more than six colors.
The work log contains no trace command, proves agent-svgtools was used to evaluate the candidate, and records a visual final assessment.
The final agent-svgtools judge combined score is at least 90 without sacrificing the structural requirements.
Human review finds the body, fins, window, and flame recognizable, correctly layered, and proportionally similar to the reference.

evals.prompt: Recreate the provided owl raster as a clean, maintainable SVG. Use agent-svgtools to evaluate and improve the result. Automatic trace may be used only as a disposable diagnostic on an isolated crop or binary silhouette; do not copy, simplify, or edit traced geometry into the final SVG. Save owl.svg and a brief worklog.md listing the commands you ran and your final assessment. You may create any other artifacts useful to your workflow. Visually verify the finished SVG.
evals.expected_output: A recognizable, visually faithful owl expressed as layered semantic vector components and deliberate curves, with enough command evidence to verify the agent-svgtools workflow and trace restriction.
expectations: The requested SVG and work log exist, and the SVG renders successfully at 500 by 500 pixels.
The SVG has a 0 0 500 500 viewBox, preserves transparency, and contains no image element, data URL, embedded raster, script, or external resource.
The SVG uses no more than 50 authored graphical elements, no more than 32 path elements, and no more than 240 path commands.
At least ten visible components have meaningful ids or belong to meaningfully named groups, and the intentional fill/stroke palette contains no more than twelve colors.
The final agent-svgtools inspect report confirms the structural, naming, palette, and vector-safety requirements rather than relying on self-reported counts.

The work log proves foreground-scoped agent-svgtools judge and visual artifacts were used, records no more than three focused revisions and two diagnostic crops, includes a visual final assessment, and shows that any trace use obeyed the diagnostic-only restriction.
The final alpha-aware foreground-scoped agent-svgtools judge combined score is at least 68 without sacrificing the structural requirements.

Human review finds the owl silhouette, paired eyes, beak, wings, belly, and feet recognizable, correctly layered, proportionally similar, and faithful to visible left/right asymmetry in the reference.
